formulas.name: previous_three_month_growth
formulas.definition: (previous 3M / the 3M before that) - 1

formulas.name: acceleration
formulas.definition: last_three_month_growth - previous_three_month_growth
formulas.edge_cases: momentum: accelerating > +5 pp, decelerating < -5 pp, otherwise stable

formulas.name: period_over_period
formulas.definition: (requested period total / previous equivalent period total) - 1

formulas.name: peak_month / trough_month
formulas.definition: calendar month with the highest / lowest mean views across the requested period

formulas.name: peak_to_average
formulas.definition: max(calendar-month means) / mean(calendar-month means)

formulas.name: trough_to_average
formulas.definition: min(calendar-month means) / mean(calendar-month means)

formulas.name: volatility
formulas.definition: pstdev(monthly views) / mean(monthly views) over the requested period
formulas.edge_cases: null with fewer than 3 months

formulas.name: views_per_unique_device
formulas.definition: pageviews / unique devices
formulas.edge_cases: unique devices are published per project only, so this is null for articles

formulas.name: coverage
formulas.definition: months with data / months in the requested period

formulas.name: topic_penetration
formulas.definition: topic views / all views of that language edition, both over the last 12 months
formulas.edge_cases: same traffic class (access, agent) for both; 'Wikipedia topic penetration', not market penetration

formulas.name: topic_share
formulas.definition: topic views in one edition / topic views across all compared editions (last 12 months)
formulas.edge_cases: relative to the compared set; editions without data are excluded and listed

formulas.name: topic_affinity
formulas.definition: (topic views / edition views) / (compared topic views / compared edition views)
formulas.edge_cases: location quotient relative to the compared editions; not an official Wikimedia metric

formulas.name: anomaly_expected
formulas.definition: better fit of median(6 months before) and median(6 months after) x seasonal factor; seasonal factor = median over other years of views / centered 12-month median, same calendar month
formulas.edge_cases: leave-one-out, so a spike cannot raise its own baseline; factor 1.0 with fewer than 2 other years

formulas.name: anomaly_flag
formulas.definition: robust z = 0.6745 x (log(actual/expected) - median) / MAD > 3.5 and |actual/expected - 1| >= 25%
formulas.edge_cases: flags in the last 3 months are provisional; cause is always 'unknown'

formulas.name: yoy_excluding_anomalies
formulas.definition: YoY with every flagged month replaced by its expected value
formulas.edge_cases: null when nothing is flagged; shows whether growth rests on one-off months (spec rule 6)

formulas.name: related_topics
formulas.definition: Wikidata P279 subclass-of (broader / reverse: narrower), P1269 facet-of (facet_of / reverse: has_facet), and text similarity (similar_content, labelled separately)
formulas.edge_cases: deduplicated with typed relations first; capped at 20; concepts without an article in the edition are skipped and counted

formulas.name: share_adjusted_yoy
formulas.definition: (1 + topic YoY) / (1 + edition YoY) - 1

formulas.name: ecosystem_signal
formulas.definition: too_small (<1,200 views/yr) > larger_category (broader or facet-of target, more views) > emerging (share-adjusted YoY >= +10%) > declining (<= -10%) > adjacent_opportunity (views >= topic) > adjacent_interest
formulas.edge_cases: adjacent interest signals only, never a claim of commercial adjacency

formulas.name: concentration_top_k
formulas.definition: views of the k largest articles / views of the topic plus its typed relations, k = 1, 5, 10, 20
formulas.edge_cases: null when the cluster has fewer than k articles; text-similar articles excluded

formulas.name: signal_market_size
formulas.definition: annual views (last 12 months): very_low < 12,000 <= low < 60,000 <= medium < 300,000 <= high < 1,500,000 <= very_high
formulas.edge_cases: absolute on purpose (spec §22), so larger editions read higher for the same topic

formulas.name: signal_growth
formulas.definition: 3-year CAGR (YoY when there is no CAGR): declining < -3% <= stable < +3% <= growing < +15% <= strongly_growing
formulas.edge_cases: raw pageviews; the explanation adds the whole edition's YoY for context

formulas.name: signal_momentum
formulas.definition: the momentum label: acceleration > +5 points accelerating, < -5 points decelerating, else stable

formulas.name: signal_localization
formulas.definition: topic affinity: weak < 0.80 <= moderate < 1.25 <= strong
formulas.edge_cases: null outside a comparison, because affinity needs other editions

formulas.name: signal_stability
formulas.definition: volatile if >= 2 anomaly episodes (runs of consecutive flagged months) and >= 1 per 12 months checked; else peak-to-average >= 1.30 highly_seasonal, >= 1.12 moderately_seasonal, else stable
formulas.edge_cases: null without 2 years of each calendar month (seasonality cannot be told from noise)

formulas.name: decision_signals
formulas.definition: five separate labels (market size, growth, momentum, localization, stability)
formulas.edge_cases: never combined into a single score, never a BUY / INVEST recommendation

formulas.name: recommendation_tier
formulas.definition: deprioritise: < 12,000 views/yr or share-adjusted YoY <= -25%; validate_first: >= 12,000 views/yr, share-adjusted YoY >= -10% and (with several options) demand >= the set's median; monitor: the rest. Within a tier, by audience size
formulas.edge_cases: evidence-based next steps from reader attention only; never a go/no-go or investment call; raw YoY when the edition total is missing

formulas.name: quadrant
formulas.definition: growth: YoY > 0; demand: annual views >= median of compared editions; labels investigate / explore / established / watch are descriptive, not recommendations

recommendation.concept: English as a second or foreign language (Wikidata Q130192)
text: No option stands out on reader attention yet.
Concept measured: English as a second or foreign language (Wikidata Q130192). A broader or narrower concept can give a different result.
No option has both a sizeable audience (12,000 views a year or more, at or above the median) and a change within 10% of its edition. Treat every option as unproven until other sources confirm demand.
Even with a niche threshold of 1,000 views a year, no option keeps pace with its edition.
Every option has under 12,000 views a year: this concept may be too narrow to measure the interest. Rerunning with a broader concept may answer the question better.

Deprioritise: es.wikipedia (only 1,389 views a year, too few to read a trend), ar.wikipedia (only 1,086 views a year, too few to read a trend), de.wikipedia (only 871 views a year, too few to read a trend), tr.wikipedia (only 832 views a year, too few to read a trend) and 2 more.

No article in pl.wikipedia: interest there can't be measured with pageviews. That gap is itself a finding (the topic isn't covered in that language), but it is not evidence of unmet demand or an untapped market, and not a reason to research that audience first. A search there finds Understanding by Design, Ortografia, Jednojęzyczny słownik dydaktyczny: search results, not matches. Ask the user whether one is the same concept before using it as a stand-in.

Basis: Wikipedia reader attention only, not revenue or product demand. This is not a go/no-go or investment call: before committing budget, confirm with search volume, app-store demand and customer interviews.

observations: es.wikipedia had the most pageviews: 1.4K in the last 12 months (29.9% of the topic's views across the compared editions).
The topic took the largest share of its edition's traffic in ar.wikipedia: 0.8 views per million.
The highest topic affinity was in ar.wikipedia: 3.30× the compared average.
Year-over-year change ranged from -52.3% (es.wikipedia) to -32.6% (de.wikipedia).
No article about this concept in: pl.wikipedia.
notes: No article about this concept in: pl (Wikidata Q130192 has no sitelink there).
Share, affinity and quadrants are computed over de, es, tr, ko, ar, id editions; left out (no article or incomplete data): pl.

pl.wikipedia has no article about this concept. A search there for 'English as a second or foreign language' finds: Understanding by Design, Ortografia, Jednojęzyczny słownik dydaktyczny. These are search results, not matches: check one is the same concept before using it as a stand-in (--topic '<title>' --language pl).
